newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER BRIBES BUSINESSMAN HOBNOBBED WITH ROYALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER BRIBES BUSINESSMAN HOBNOBBED WITH ROYALS.

text.p: Heng Suan Lim, a Malaysian businessman accused of paying English soccer stars to rig matches, spent much of his youth in an orphanage but ended up enjoying the company of royals.
Lim told a court on Monday his friends and business contacts included members of the Malaysian and Brunei royal families as well as the cream of the Far East.

"I felt I needed a strong contact base to extend my career. I associated with the heads of corporations, chief executives of banks, contractors, politicians and the royal family of Malaysia," he said when questioned by his lawyer Jerome Lynch.
Malaysia has nine royal families. Under the country's unique rotating monarchy, the nine sultans take turns every five years being king.

Lim said that in 1993 he put together a 100,000 pound ($160,000) deal to print the Malaysian royal family's Christmas cards. He also supplied a luxury Bentley car to the Brunei royal family for 122,000 pounds.

Lim, along with former striker John Fashanu, is accused of paying one-time Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar to rig matches. The two men are also accused of running a similar scheme with former Wimbledon goalkeeper Hans Segers.
All four defendants deny the charges, although Lim admitted he had helped the syndicate forecast matches with the help of insider information from Fashanu, Segers and Grobbelaar.

On Tuesday, Lynch is due to question him on the more than 500,000 pounds which was transferred to him from bank accounts in Asia. The prosecution says Lim has never managed to satisfactorily explain where the money came from.

When police arrested Lim in March 1995 they found a large plastic folder with the business cards of friends and business partners. Lim asked for the names not to be read out in court, saying otherwise he would be treated as outcasts in Malaysia.
Lynch then flicked through the cards, leaving out names but reading out occupations such as minister, director, chairman, manager, judge and aide to a royal family.
"It has caused me great embarrassment. I wouldn't even think of asking them here to testify on my behalf because it's an unfair burden on my friends," Lim said.
Asked to identify one person who telephone records showed he had called 158 times over two years, Lim replied: "He was attached to the royal family of Brunei."

He said some members of the Malaysian royal family had attended his sister's wedding in January 1993. Lynch produced a?????eal of new identity, because I came from a broken home. I felt very proud of my identity through soccer," he said.
He and his two sisters went back to their mother after she scraped together enough money to rent an apartment.
